question.text: Navya Agritech reports 320 farmers received drip-irrigation kits. The SIA wants to test 'additionality' (deadweight). Which procedure is MOST effective?

answer.text: Compare to a pre-intervention baseline and, where feasible, to a matched control group of farmers who did not receive the kits
Accept the SE's self-reported assumption that 100% of outcomes are attributable
Measure only the photographic evidence of kit distribution

explanation.text: The Logic: Deadweight is the 'what would have happened anyway' baseline. The gold standard is a matched control-group comparison; failing that, a robust pre-intervention baseline. Self-reporting (B), photos (C), and SROI without baseline (D) all fail the deadweight test. The Trap: Option B is precisely the error flagged in Chapter 7.4 (unreliable assumption-based reporting). Option C confuses evidence of distribution with evidence of impact. Cross-Exam Context: Control-group methodology (RCT) is the J-PAL / DIME standard cited in Ch 7.2.2. Assessor's Pro-Tip: If a control group is infeasible, use a difference-in-differences design across two blocks (one with intervention, one without), and explicitly document the DiD assumption. That's assurable. Photos and self-reporting alone are not.
